translation_direction: de → vi; direct from the specifically identified complete German electronic witness
ai_disclosure: Direct AI-produced Vietnamese prose by Claude Opus 5.5. The drafting system conducted the final full assessment; a separate-context assessment by the same model family read every pair and supplied findings first. No human translator, editor, reviewer, independent model consensus or actual reader feedback is recorded.

entry_conditions: Complete named-source and Vietnamese texts, explicit alignment and exact content hashes.
Compare every source and target passage; disclose that this assessor also revised the text and has seen earlier AI assessments.
Source and target edition titles are present and compared explicitly; the title review must match both catalog title strings exactly.
exit_conditions: One complete AI review with a weighted score at least 8.6 using the five unchanged weights and half-point category scores; no separate numerical dimension floors.
All canonical passages reviewed; no unresolved major or critical finding; source and target hashes match the final text.
Publication and rights status are recorded separately in the edition catalog; an AI score does not supply a license.
The selected review includes source_title, target_title and a substantive title rationale; changed titles require a fresh matching review.
review_process.human_feedback: Optional after publication or while a work remains a draft; no prior human publication review is required by v2.

decisions.decision: Schiller’s Sturm und Drang rhetoric is kept as vivid, excessive Vietnamese; the robbers’ speech is crude and lively; Franz’s cold smoothness keeps its calculation.
decisions.rationale: The play is its rhetorical excess and the contrast of the brothers.

decisions.decision: The German text comes from Project Gutenberg #47804; the preface is included as its own section.
Spiegelberg’s antisemitic phrase at unit 458 is rendered faithfully as the source’s content, not softened; it stands in the speaker’s voice, not the translator’s.
decisions.rationale: Silent softening would change the text; the editor should confirm.

revision_history.scope: Complete initial direct translation, separate-context full source/target assessment and concrete revisions before the selected final review.

changes.explanation: Franz’s reading of Karl’s letter called the elder brother “em trai”; now “anh trai”, the sibling seniority of the German.
Same sibling error in Franz’s soliloquy (“Đó là anh trai ngươi!”).
The salutation “Unglücklicher Bruder!” was addressed to the elder Karl; now “Người anh bất hạnh”.
“Auskeuchte” (expired) was rendered as sneezing; corrected.
Amalia’s “Bruder meines Karls” made Franz the elder brother; now “Em trai của Karl”.
The insult “Kastraten-Jahrhundert” lost its central word; restored as “thái giám”.
“Even if half an Our Father” was inverted to “unless”; corrected.
Steps “staggering forward” were rendered as stepping back; corrected.
Amalia’s “Mein, mein!” (mine, mine) was rendered as a denial; now “Của em”.
The antisemitic phrase of Spiegelberg is kept as the source’s content (“làm ăn kiểu Do Thái”), not softened; the editor should confirm this choice.
“Block” as the execution block was rendered as a mat; now a chopping block.
Nachtigall (nightingale) was rendered as a skylark; now họa mi.
“Man vermißt ihn” (he is missed) was rendered as remembering him; corrected.
“Geadelt” (ennobled) was rendered as canonised; corrected.
“Hutschnur” is a hat cord, not a watch chain; corrected.
“Weib” as Moor’s cold address to Amalia had been tender; corrected.
The direction of the avenger was reversed; Franz is to go out to meet him. Corrected.
“Poche dem Tyrannen-Verhängniß” (defy the tyrant’s fate) was rendered as knocking; corrected.
Franz’s “em trai” for Karl, the elder brother, corrected to “anh trai”.
The same sibling reversal at Prag, corrected.
“Mein Bruder” for Karl, corrected to “anh trai của con”.
The relative clause whose subject is freedom’s name had been attached to the men; now attached to tự do.
“Ihn und Ihn” (two men) was rendered as one; corrected.
“Versicherte” (secured) was rendered as bribed; corrected.
“Bettelvögten” (beggar-wardens) was rendered as beggars; corrected.
“Fanger” is a bird-catcher, not a gardener; corrected.
“Bräutigam” (groom) was dropped, leaving the reply without an antecedent; restored.
Minor sense and register fixes in Act II, applied after checking the German.
Minor phrasing fixes in Act V, applied after checking the German.

selection_limit: Chosen for a complete, directly sourced and openly reusable Vietnamese edition. Existing Vietnamese translations, their quality and reader demand have not been comprehensively assessed; no absence or superiority claim is made.

glossary.draft_rendering: anh / em (fixed); Karl to the band: ngươi / ta
glossary.rationale: The lovers’ pair is stable; the robber band’s register is harsher.

glossary.draft_rendering: Karl: anh trai (elder); Franz: em trai (younger)
glossary.rationale: Karl is the elder son; every sibling reference follows that.
One term for the robber chief.

witness_decision: Selected Project Gutenberg #47804, an electronic transcription of Die Räuber: Ein Schauspiel from the 1781 text. The Gutenberg page does not name the exact printing and the text was not collated with the first edition.

title_review.rationale: The title is rendered as ‘Bọn cướp’ (The Robbers); no earlier Vietnamese title was checked.

passage_assessment_notes.assessment: Franz reads Karl’s letter aloud; the Leipzig correspondent’s letter.
Moor’s last defiance before his death.
